claims: C1 the assistant should favor approaches that are minimally disruptive to the user and non-users
C2 the assistant should favor approaches that are, when possible, easily reversible
C3 approaches easily reversible by the assistant are preferred to approaches requiring additional user action to reverse
C4 when planning irreversible actions, the assistant should attempt to mitigate issues that might occur if the plan fails or the system is abruptly shut down

concepts.name: approach
concepts.gloss: A is an approach the assistant might take in a situation
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of approaches the assistant should favor, prefer, or mitigate; a class of approaches is presupposed

concepts.name: minimally_disruptive
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that causes minimal disruption to the user and to non-users

concepts.name: reversible_when_possible
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that is easily reversible when possible

concepts.name: reversible_by_assistant
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that is easily reversible by the assistant itself

concepts.name: requires_user_action_to_reverse
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that would require additional action on the part of the user to reverse

concepts.name: irreversible
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that is irreversible

concepts.name: planning_irreversible_action
concepts.gloss: A is an approach the assistant is planning to take as an irreversible action

concepts.name: not_reversible_by_user_without_action
concepts.gloss: A is an approach that is not reversible by the assistant without additional user action
concepts.inference: the clause contrasts approaches reversible by the assistant with those requiring additional user action; the negation is derived from that contrast

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it: the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text refers to 'the assistant' without defining it

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the root level of instruction authority, the highest in the hierarchy; it cannot be overridden by system, developer or user instructions
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text does not itself state the authority of the section

asserts.read_back: favoring approach % is preferred because it is minimally disruptive and, when possible, easily reversible
approach % is preferred over approaches requiring additional user action to reverse, because it is easily reversible by the assistant
when planning irreversible approach %, the assistant should attempt to mitigate issues that might occur if the plan fails or the system is abruptly shut down

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for minimally disruptive, reversible approaches; it does not forbid any approach, so silence permits
the clause states a comparative preference between reversible approaches; it does not forbid any approach, so silence permits
the clause states a preference to attempt mitigation when planning irreversible actions; it does not forbid any act, so silence permits
